title: Makefile builds/checks a debug XCFramework while Tuist manifests require release
reasoning: The generated Xcode project points both the app and GhostwriterClient at the release EpilogueShared.xcframework, but the Makefile prerequisite only proves the debug XCFramework exists. On a clean or partially cleaned workspace where the debug artifact exists but release is absent, `make generate` and `make build` skip rebuilding the shared framework and then generate/build a project with missing release framework references. The README also documents plain `tuist generate`/`tuist build`, which does not create either artifact first.
reproduction: Remove ../shared/build/XCFrameworks/release/EpilogueShared.xcframework while leaving ../shared/build/XCFrameworks/debug/EpilogueShared.xcframework present, then run `make generate` or `make build`; the Makefile prerequisite is satisfied even though the manifest-referenced framework is missing.
recommendation: Use one configuration consistently. Either make manifests point at the debug XCFramework for debug workflows and release for release workflows, or change the Makefile prerequisite to the release path and invoke the Gradle task that guarantees that release artifact exists. Also update README setup/build commands to use the wrapper that builds the required XCFramework first.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests or CI command in this feature exercises a clean setup/build path or asserts that manifest .xcframework paths exist after the Makefile prerequisite runs.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a lightweight build-config smoke check that runs the XCFramework Makefile target in a clean artifact directory and verifies every `.xcframework(path:)` referenced by Tuist manifests exists before `tuist generate`.
minimumFixScope: Align `Makefile` `XCFRAMEWORK_DIR`/Gradle task with the release paths in `App/Project.swift` and `Modules/GhostwriterClient/Project.swift`, or parameterize the manifests and wrapper so debug/release paths are selected coherently.
